titulo: MCP Apps: interface inside the client (official extension)
lead: Sometimes text is not enough: a list with colors, a chart, a form. MCP Apps is the official extension that links a tool to an HTML page that the client draws in an isolated iframe. In this lesson you link a panel to the ver_turmas tool and check the link without needing to open a client.
objetivo: link an HTML interface to a tool with MCP Apps and check the link through the Inspector, without opening any client.

aprende.t: Tool + ui:// resource + isolated iframe in the client
registerAppTool and registerAppResource from the ext-apps 2.0.3 package
A client without support gets the text; CSP restricts the page's network

hero_alt: Dark monitor with a chat window and a small panel with a list and bars inside, connected to a mini server.

secoes.titulo: How the panel reaches the chat

nos.detalhe: ver_turmas declares _meta: { ui: { resourceUri: 'ui://turmas/painel.html' } }. The rest is an ordinary tool.
The panel's HTML is served as a resource with the type text/html;profile=mcp-app.
The model calls the tool like any other. The client sees the resourceUri and fetches the HTML.
The client draws the HTML in a sandboxed iframe and hands over the tool result through messages. External network only with a declared csp.

secoes.legenda: MCP Apps is the first official MCP extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui), announced on 01/26/2026 with support in Claude (web and desktop), Goose, and VS Code Insiders.

secoes.sub: app.mjs reuses the class server and adds a tool with an interface.

secoes.titulo: A demo shortcut, called what it is
paragrafos: To keep the page in a single HTML file, with no build, the kit embeds the package's app-with-deps.js and swaps the final export for a constant. It works with the ext-apps 2.0.3 that the kit pins; in a newer version it may break.
In a real project, follow the official MCP Apps quickstart (a page with a bundler, or the ready-made templates in the ext-apps repository).

secoes.titulo: Check the link with the Inspector
secoes.sub: --app-info reads each tool's interface metadata without calling any of them.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.11.0 --cli node app.mjs --method tools/list --app-info
echo "saída: $?"

perguntas.p: How does a tool tell the client it has an interface?
opcoes: Returning the entire interface HTML in the content field
Through the Mcp-Name header sent along with each HTTP call
With _meta.ui.resourceUri pointing to a ui:// resource
perguntas.explica: The link is the resourceUri; the HTML is a separate resource, with the type text/html;profile=mcp-app.

perguntas.p: The client does not support MCP Apps. What happens with ver_turmas?
opcoes: The call fails with an error and the model tries another tool
It works as a regular tool and returns the text
The server refuses this client's connection right at discover
The model does not see the tool
perguntas.explica: The interface is an extra. Without support, the client uses the content and the structuredContent as with any tool.

opcoes: On the server, generating an image
In an isolated iframe inside the client
In a new browser tab, outside the client
perguntas.explica: The client draws the HTML in a sandboxed iframe; external network only with a csp declared by the server.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit say that embedding the bundle is a shortcut?
opcoes: It depends on the internal name in build 2.0.3 and may break on another version
Because the MCP Apps specification forbids embedding JavaScript in the HTML
Because it makes the server much slower on every resource read
Because it does not work on Node 20
perguntas.explica: The trick swaps the final export of the packaged file. For a real project, use the official quickstart with a bundler.

itens.texto: _meta.ui.resourceUri on the tool; HTML as a ui:// resource.
Draws in an isolated iframe; without support, text only.
